newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour slams Anglian on job cuts.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour slams Anglian on job cuts.

text.p: British utility Anglian Water's plans to slash up to 300 jobs as part of a review aimed at saving 10 million stg a year were slammed by the opposition Labour party as evidence that privatisation benefits only a few at the top.

The cuts were "another disgraceful example of how privatisation of the utilities has benefitted a few at the top, with staff and customer service paying the price",Labour employment spokesman Ian McCartney said.
Anglian said it would make a provision of 20 million stg to cover the cuts, most of which will be voluntary.
Anglian is based in Huntingdon, in the constituency of Prime Minister John Major.

Labour, which is ahead of the ruling Conservatives in polls with an election due by May, has promised to levy a one-off "windfall" tax on privatised utilities to pay for a programme to move 250,000 young people into work.
Anglian was privatised along with the rest of Britain's water and sewerage industry in 1989.
